text:
Alex: Ran a high-concurrency nsys pressure run on the batching+KV hotpath this morning. Wanted to share quick notes before I forget :coffee:

Alex: Command I used (short run for repro, ~30s steady-state window after warmup):
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o /tmp/nsys/press_run --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=stop --stop=30s --force --snapshot=on 
# started the server, then triggered 200 concurrent requests with the load script
```

Alex: Key flags: trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt to get kernel timeline + our NVTX brackets + OSRT thread scheduling. --sample=none to avoid CPU sampling noise; we rely on timeline/kernels. Used --stop to limit file size.

Mira: Nice. Did you bracket warmup explicitly with NVTX? We saw noise when warmup overlapped capture last week.

Alex: Yep, load script emits NVTX: push("warmup-start") ... pop and then push("steady-start") before measured phase. Also used OSRT so we can correlate GPU kernel launches to our runtime threads.

Sam: Any surprising hotspots?

Alex: Two main things: 1) attention kernel switches on long sequences (transformer_attention_fwd vs transformer_attention_bwd) kept flipping; cost of kernel-selection path was visible as micro stalls. 2) KV-cache eviction path: when concurrent batches hit the same KV shard we saw serialized CPU work (locking) showing up as CPU OSRT preemption spikes which delayed subsequent kernel launches.

Priya: Do you have the kernel timeline snippet? Could paste a 6-10s sample.

Alex: Pasted a tiny excerpt of the nvprof-style timeline in text form (trimmed):
```
[GPU time 0ms] kernel: grouped_gemm_fp16  (20 us)
[GPU time 2ms] kernel: transformer_attention_fwd  (1.2 ms)
[GPU time 3.5ms] kernel: transformer_attention_fwd_qk  (0.9 ms)
[GPU time 5ms] kernel: cutlass_gemm_agg_fp16  (0.6 ms)
[.. repeated pattern ..]
# then a gap with no GPU kernels ~2.4ms, while OSRT shows thread context switch on runtime-thread-7
[GPU resume] kernel: grouped_gemm_fp16  (18 us)
```

Mira: That gap+context-switch sounds like a batching heuristic failure: runtime decided to wait for more tokens then got preempted. Can you check if our batching timeout bumped up in that run?

Alex: Batching config: max_batch=8, batch_wait_ms=3. We expect small wait_ms to keep latency bounded. On the trace the runtime tried to coalesce 3 requests then waited until the 3ms timer fired; but due to KV-lock on CPU it missed the timer and the OSRT preemption added ~2ms.

Sam: So two levers: reduce batch_wait_ms for this customer class, or make KV-lock async so launch path isn't blocked on CPU.

Priya: Also check kernel selection heuristics — if attention_fwd variant A is better for batch sizes 1-4 and variant B for >=8, but we mis-predict at steady-state, you get repeated kernel switching overhead. Alex, can you capture nvtx markers around the kernel-selection decision?

Alex: Yup added NVTX around select_kernel() in the next run. Also marked which kernel name chosen. Results looked like: select_kernel took ~70-120us on each decision and we toggled variants when input seq_len jumped from 64 -> 96. That decision cost is non-trivial at high QPS.

perf-bot: FYI, large qdrep (120MB) uploaded to /artifacts/nsys/2798765432-press_run.qdrep :eyes:

Mira: Good. For immediate mitigation: Sam's suggestion to reduce batch_wait_ms to 1ms for latency-sensitive routes. For longer term: move KV eviction off the hot launch path and add a fast-path try-lock to avoid blocking.

Alex: Agreed. Will spin a short A/B: batch_wait_ms=1ms vs 3ms and run same nsys profile to compare tail. Also will try place kernel_select NVTX markers and measure select_kernel time per invocation.

Sam: When you run again, also add `--sample=cpu` for one run to get thread stack traces for the blocking periods — but keep sample=none for the main timeline to keep low overhead.

Alex: Will do. Uploading trimmed timeline and a small perf report shortly. Thanks all :rocket:
